Definition: properly, a failure; by implication nothing; usually (adverb) not at all; also lest
BiblicalUsage: Bal is the small word for not, nothing, never, lest. It shows up wherever Scripture draws a hard line: the wicked says in his pride that there is no God, the earth is established so it cannot be moved, and the foundations of the world are laid so they will not be removed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this little word carries enormous weight, because what God says will not happen cannot happen. The psalmist leans on it the way a man leans on a wall: the Lord reigns, the world stands, and no scheming of the wicked can undo what God has fixed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
